facts.statement: Kangnasaurus was named in 1915 by Sidney H. Haughton.
facts.quote: Kangnasaurus was named in 1915 by Sidney H. Haughton.

facts.statement: The genus name Kangnasaurus refers to Kangnas farm, and the species name coetzeei honors the farmer Coetzee.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Kangnas farm; the specific name to the farmer, Coetzee.

facts.statement: The holotype, SAM 2732, is a tooth found at a depth of 34 meters in a well at Farm Kangnas in the Orange River valley of northern Cape Province, South Africa.
facts.quote: Kangnasaurus is based on holotype SAM 2732, a tooth found at a depth of 34 metres in a well at Farm Kangnas, in the Orange River valley of northern Cape Province, South Africa.

facts.statement: Haughton described several other fossils possibly belonging to Kangnasaurus, including partial thigh bones, shin bones, a metatarsal, vertebrae, and unidentified bones.
facts.quote: Haughton described several other fossils as possibly belonging to Kangnasaurus. These include five partial thigh bones, a partial thigh bone and shin bone, a partial metatarsal, a partial shin and foot, vertebrae, and unidentified bones.

facts.statement: More recent studies have placed Kangnasaurus within the elasmarian group.
facts.quote: However, more recent studies have separately uncovered a position nested within the elasmarian group.

facts.statement: Kangnasaurus is usually considered a dubious genus, though a 2007 review by Ruiz-Omeñaca and colleagues retained it as potentially valid, differing from other dryosaurids by details of the thigh bone.
facts.quote: Kangnasaurus es usualmente considerado como un género dudoso, aunque una revisión de 2007 de los driosáuridos por Ruiz-Omeñaca y colaboradores lo retiene como potencialmente válido, difiriendo de otros driosáuridos por detalles del fémur.

facts.statement: Kangnasaurus is known from remains dating between the middle-Campanian and Maastrichtian periods.
facts.quote: It is known from a tooth and possibly some postcranial remains dating between the middle-Campanian to Maastrichtian Kalahari Deposits Formation.

facts.statement: Sedimentological analyses suggest a Late Cretaceous age between the Campanian and Maastrichtian is more likely than an Early Cretaceous age.
facts.quote: But a Late Cretaceous age between the Campanian and Maastrichtian is more likely due to sedimentological analyses.

facts.statement: Some sources suggest Kangnasaurus lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 134 million years ago during the Valanginian, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 134 millones de años durante el Valanginiense, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Kangnasaurus as Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other basal iguanodontians, Kangnasaurus would have been a bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Like other basal iguanodontians, it would have been a bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: It is debated whether additional fossils described by Haughton and Cooper actually belong to Kangnasaurus, as some bones may have come from other deposits.
facts.quote: Some of the bones apparently came from other deposits, and Haughton was not certain that they all belonged to his new genus. Cooper was also not certain, but described the other specimens as if they did belong to Kangnasaurus.
